item.title: Intro
item.description:
Source: TW

On the South Indian Brahma-yāmala supplement

The South Indian Brahma-yāmala supplement (hereinafter, BY-SI) has 51 chapters (paṭala-s), of which 49 have come down to us, albeit in a somewhat corrupt and lacunose fashion. The 51st chapter is incomplete. The BY-SI chapters show variations in their colophons. The most common one takes the form:

  • brahma-yāmale śata-sahasra-saṃhitāyām <X>-nāma <N> paṭalaḥ |

This suggests that it saw itself as part of a greater “Brahma-yāmala” of a 100,000 verses. Keeping with this, internally, the BY-SI explicitly associates its ritualists with the knowers of the Brahma-yāmala:

item.title: South indian ekavIrI
item.description:
Source: TW

The installation of this goddess ekavIrI, an ectype of chAmuNDA, indicates that in the high point of the choLa-s, a millennium ago, worship was being performed as per the South Indian supplement of brahmayAmala tantra. This goddess is a unique hallmark of that tantra:

sarvāṅgaṃ tu nyasen mantrī
ekavīrī-śarīrataḥ |
brāhmī māheśvarī caiva
kaumārī vaiṣṇavī tathā ||
vārāhī caiva māhendrī
vīrabhadra-gaṇādhipau |
ekavīrī śarīre tu
vinyased vaikamudrayā ||

The mantrin should perform nyāsa on all the limbs, [projecting them] from the body of Ekavīrī. Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, and likewise Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, Vārāhī and Māhendrī, and [the pair] Vīrabhadra and Gaṇādhipa. [All these] he should place within the body of Ekavīrī, or [alternatively do the nyāsa] with the single mudrā. (South Indian “brahma-yAmala”)
